changes.title: check.sh crashed outside a git checkout
changes.problem: The repository was taken out of git to become a project of its own; check.sh then failed on git commands with no clear reason, and check-all.sh refused to prove the tree at all.
changes.fix: lib/check.py (check.sh and check-all.sh are its doors) asks first whether the project is a git checkout: check.sh stops with exit 2 and says to run git init and commit; check-all.sh still runs every step for proof and writes no release certificate.

changes.title: The guards named one product's parts in their code
changes.problem: impact.py, run.sh, the gate, the certificate, setup and the audit named a backend, a frontend and their tools in code, so every other product had to edit the framework itself.
changes.fix: One configuration, crissp/testsuite/suites.json (lib/project.py), describes the product's steps (folder, command, coverage, gate), what a change runs (paths), its shared ground, setup and audit; every guard reads it, and run.py runs the steps.

changes.title: The tools found the project from their own file location
changes.problem: Every library reached the repository's root with Path(__file__).parents[n], so the engine could not live apart from a project's data.
changes.fix: The project is CRISSP_ROOT or the current directory (the scripts export CRISSP_ROOT); only the engine's own files (the dashboard page, the look, the UX page) are found next to the code.

changes.title: The Tests dashboard and the UX suite looked different and ran apart
changes.problem: The dashboard and the UX suite had their own looks, ports and servers, and nothing linked an approved design to the PBI it became.
changes.fix: One local server (lib/serve.py) serves /dashboard/, /ux/ and the shared look in crissp/look (tokens, font, theme, water), and nothing else of the repository; an approved design becomes a PBI through the crissp tool, and the board links it back.

gaps: No browser test of the framework's own pages: the dashboard's and the UX suite's JavaScript (app.js, ux.js, look.js) run only in a person's browser; the tests prove the data and the server behind them.
The UX team's rounds and designs are headless Claude Code runs and its screenshots need Playwright's Chromium: both are stood in by the tests, no real round has been proven by a test.
The deploy step needs helm (and terraform for its fmt and validate) on the machine; without terraform that part is skipped with a visible line, not proven.
The CVE audit needs the network (uv resolves the pinned tools, pip-audit asks the advisories): offline the audit step is red, never green.
Without git there is no release certificate: check.sh stops and check-all.sh proves the tree but certifies nothing until the repository has commits.
The coverage baseline starts empty: the first green full run with a commit sets it, and until then the rule that every changed line is covered is skipped.
